newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada spot natgas prices mixed, exports climb.
newsitem.headline: Canada spot natgas prices mixed, exports climb.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices were mixed on Wednesday with most domestic points holding recent levels and exports to the western United States climbing sharply from last week.
Spot gas at Alberta's AECO storage hub was quoted at C$1.93/1.98 per gigajoule, up one cent from last week. Gas for January delivery was talked at C$2 to C$2.05 per GJ.

Over the past week, field receipts on the NOVA Alberta pipeline network dropped by about 300 million cubic feet per day, which pushed storage withdrawals to 1.1 billion cubic feet per day on Tuesday, said a Calgary-based trader.
He said AECO prices were likely to be pressured over the next few days with forecasts for above-normal temperatures through Sunday.
However, prices could be kept high as players attempt to honor commitments and make new deals for gas after the recent string of small-marketer bankruptcies. "That's the wild card," he said.

At the borders, prices at Huntington/Sumas jumped as high as US$3.50 per million British thermal units because of high demand in California and the U.S. Pacific Northwest, where stormy weather conditions prevailed, traders said. ((Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
